title: Cage Excel meta-row adapter contract v1
description: The two JSON messages between `cage` and a user-supplied Excel meta-row decoding script (decision record: docs/design.md section 51, X-series). One file carries both directions; the top-level oneOf accepts either a request (cage -> script) or a response (script -> cage). Vocabulary is the Cage Schema DSL field name set (T3.1); the adapter may not invent rule semantics.

request.description: Read on stdin by the script. The full sheet grid is supplied so the script may locate convention rows wherever the author puts them.

contract.description: Contract version. Cage and the script both check it; an unknown version fails loudly.

workbook.description: Workbook path relative to the project root, as declared in [source_roots].

sheet.description: Sheet name that is being decoded. Hidden and very-hidden sheets never reach the adapter (docs/design.md section 3.1 ruling).

header_row.description: 0-based index of the data header row exactly as Cage resolved it for this workbook (the [source.excel].header_row knob, default 0). Informational: the script decides where the data header really is and answers in response.header_row.

grid.description: The whole visible sheet as rows of cells, 0-based in both directions. Cell = integer, non-integer number, string, boolean, or null. An empty cell is null. A merged cell is back-filled to the top-left value (xlsx only, .ods never). A date or datetime cell is sent as the same form the data plane renders it in — the Debug form of the Excel serial (ExcelDateTime { value: 44927.0, datetime_type: DateTime, is_1904: false }), not a normalized ISO-8601 string. ISO-shaped cells the spreadsheet already stored as text arrive verbatim as strings. Formula cells carry their cached value; nothing is re-evaluated (the same policy as [source.excel].eval_formulas=false).

config.description: The contents of the [source.excel].script_config table, verbatim. The script reads its own tuning here, so no new cage knobs are needed to pass options through.

response.description: Read from stdout by Cage. This is the only channel through which a script can influence the build: it is validated against this schema and then against the vocabulary table (unknown keywords and out-of-vocabulary literals fail, E2202). It is never interpreted as code.

table.description: The table name the decoded metadata applies to. Must match the table Cage resolves for this sheet.

header_row.description: 0-based index of the row that carries the data column names. Everything Cage treats as convention must sit above it (built-in presets A and B include it in the same index space).

columns.description: Per-column metadata, keyed by the data column name. Column-level only in v1: no cross-table rules, no expression rules, no L7 game rules (those stay in the Schema DSL and the validation layers).

column.description: One column's declared convention. Every key is a Cage Schema DSL field name (T3.1, the same set as JSON Schema's core keywords where they overlap) - the adapter layer invents no vocabulary. `cell` anchors the declaration so any diagnostic points at the exact cell.

cell.description: A1-style address inside the decoded sheet, e.g. "B2" or "G27". Where a column-level rule has no single anchor (a keyword row whose value is spread across columns), the keyword cell is used.

primary_key.description: Schema DSL name, unchanged. Mapping a column's primary_key to the table-level `primary_key` list happens on the Schema side, not here.

default.description: Schema DSL name, unchanged. A JSON literal: null, boolean, string, number, an array, or an object. The six branches are the six JSON Schema types, which are mutually exclusive, so exactly one can match a given default.

enum.description: Schema DSL name, unchanged. A literal value list; use `type` = "Enum<Name>" when the value set is itself a named enumeration.

min.description: Schema DSL name, unchanged (the "range" of the earlier discussion is min/max).

reference.description: Schema DSL name, unchanged - the same object the Schema field reference accepts. Declaring the reference column is metadata; resolving and checking it is the validation layers' job. `predicate` is deliberately not part of the contract: a reference declared in a meta row points at a table and a field, and any additional predicate belongs in the Schema.

description.description: Schema DSL name, unchanged (the "comment" convention row of the A/B presets maps here).

targets.description: Schema DSL name, unchanged - the column's client/server grouping is a plain Schema declaration, not a new concept here.

field_type.description: The value of a column's `type`. This is the Cage Schema field's own `type` slot, verbatim - the adjacently tagged `{ kind, value }` object form that `FieldType` deserializes, one of its 19 kinds. The contract deliberately carries the exact shape the Schema accepts rather than inventing a shorthand (there is no translation step between the contract and the schema, so there is no place for the two spellings to drift). Scalars carry no `value`; `Array` and `Enum` carry a `value`; `Object` carries a property map; `Map` carries `{ key_type, value_type }`.
